messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty Alert PGRD-4532 fired for tenant 'ApexMed' (service: reserved-inference-apexmed). Symptoms: sustained p95 latency > 2.5s and error rate > 2%. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PGRD-4532 - runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/reserved-pool

mike_oncall: Ack. I'm on it, pulling dashboards and logs now.

alex_prod: seeing p95 ~3.8s, error-rate ~4.1% over the last 3m. Reserved pool util 100%, queue length ~120. KV-cache eviction spikes coincident with latency. sample trace id: trace-apx-0a1b2c

sara_dev: no recent model deploys for ApexMed (last deploy 48h ago). No config rolls either.

oncall-bot: Auto-escalation scheduled in 5m if unresolved. Next escalation path: L2 -> EngSRE.

mike_oncall: Starting mitigation: bump reserved pool nodes +2. Command:```
# rwdctl CLI
rwdctl reserved scale --tenant apexmed --add 2 --region us-west-2
```Estimated spin-up ~90s. I'll also enable overflow routing to shared pool for new requests.

incident-bot: Scale action acknowledged. Scaling job id: scale-8732. Expected ready in ~1m30s. Overflow routing: enabled -> route-fallback:shared-hosted.

alex_prod: I pushed a quick kvcache config revert — we had an aggressive eviction threshold yesterday. Before: `kv.eviction_threshold: 0.6` -> reverted to default `0.95`. Snippet:```yaml
kv: 
  eviction_threshold: 0.95
  warmup_seconds: 30
```

sara_dev: logs:```
[2025-03-21T09:12:03Z] ERROR kv_cache evict_rate=480/s tenant=apexmed trace=trace-apx-0a1b2c msg="mass eviction triggered"
[2025-03-21T09:12:04Z] WARN request_queue backlog=118 svc=reserved-inference-apexmed
```

priya_se: Customer impact estimate? do we have % of requests failing or timing out? I pinged @amy_csm to notify customer and CSM team.

amy_csm: Amy here, ping received. ApexMed on-call is already aware, CSM inbox flagged. Customer seeing timeouts in UI and increased retries. They reported increased error rate starting ~09:09Z.

mike_oncall: Quick metrics update: 60s after scale + kv revert -> p95 down to 1.7s, error-rate down to 0.8%. Queue drained to ~18. Monitoring for stability. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Alert PGRD-4532 acknowledged by mike_oncall at 173999... (ack).

incident-bot: Note: if error-rate rises above 1% for 3 consecutive minutes, auto-escalate to L2 and trigger page to eng-sre-primary. Also captured snapshot: metrics/snapshot/1739999999-apexmed.json

mike_oncall: Follow-ups I'm doing now: 1) keep extra +2 nodes for 15m, 2) leave overflow routing enabled for 10m, 3) add temp alert to reduce kv eviction aggressiveness, 4) collect traces for root-cause.

priya_se: Handing off after monitoring window — I'm taking responsibility at 04:00UTC handoff. Steps documented in this thread and I added notes to the runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/reserved-pool#apexmed. Also recommending a post-incident follow-up with infra to evaluate long-running kv-cache tuning.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: outgoing=mike_oncall, incoming=priya_se, handoff_ts=1740000100.

priya_se: Acked. I'll keep watch for the next 30m. If anything re-surges I'll escalate and open a postmortem if we see recurrence. For now customer impact estimated ~6% of requests experienced >3s or 5xx during the spike. CSM notified (amy_csm).

mike_oncall: Closing immediate mitigation. I'll rollback the temporary nodes in 15m if steady. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident PGRD-4532 marked: mitigation_in_progress -> monitoring. Please keep thread updated with any customer callbacks or metrics regressions.

priya_se: adding entry for post-incident: owner=priya_se, severity=sev3, customer=ApexMed, impact_summary="intermittent high p95 and kv eviction led to ~6% 5xx/timeouts for ~6 minutes", next_steps=[tune-kv, evaluate autoscale headroom, consider pre-warm for high-load windows].

amy_csm: I'll prep a customer-facing note summarizing impact and mitigation; will coordinate with legal if SLA credit requested.

mike_oncall: ping if anything pops. otherwise will update ticket and close alert in 30m.

incident-bot: :information_source: Reminder: attach relevant traces and segment of logs to the incident ticket for the post-incident review.
